headline: 20-year power purchase agreement for wood pyrolysis project at McNeil recommended to council
summary: Vermont Renewable Gas proposed a 2.2 MW wood pyrolysis unit at McNeil that would produce about 18,480 MWh a year, roughly 5.5% of Burlington Electric's load. The 20-year contract includes a buyout option in year seven, and the general manager's estimate is about a 60% cut in stack CO2 compared with traditional combustion at McNeil. The recommendation carried 4 to 1. Items 4.3 and 4.5 were postponed to December 7th, and the 405 Pine Street lease was recommended for council approval.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda and the actions listed in it, unanimously.
Approved the HR packet, moving a dispatch position to Winooski One and a billing position to a smart grid engineer role, unanimously.
Recommended to the city council a 20-year power purchase agreement for a wood pyrolysis demonstration project at McNeil, 4 to 1.
Postponed items 4.3 and 4.5 to December 7th, unanimously.
Recommended council approval of signing a lease at 405 Pine Street, unanimously, subject to City Attorney review.
discussion: Pyrolysis economics and risk: Members asked for ratepayer impact figures and price comparisons with other sources. The general manager said cost was not the main driver and that the developer would carry the risks of permitting, financing, construction, and operations.

Stack emissions with McNeil: Members asked whether combined emissions from both units would fall. The general manager said the new unit would use wood that would otherwise be burned at McNeil, and members asked for emissions projections in writing.
Public comment against the project: Speakers said the project would add greenhouse gases and hazardous air pollutants, and urged alternatives to McNeil.

Success metrics and McNeil's role: Members asked how success would be measured, including stack CO2, reliability, and biochar use. The general manager said the goal is not to simply turn McNeil off, but to move toward better technologies.

405 Pine Street lease: The BCA director said the Burlington City Arts Foundation owns the building, and the city's space would grow from 7,700 to 16,257 square feet. A member asked whether new revenue covers the cost increase, and the director said it essentially does.
